newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen steady to soft amid soft crude.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen steady to soft amid soft crude.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices were seen to be steady to soft on the back of lower crudes, traders said on Tuesday.

A local trader said he would be willing to sell September-loading barrels at $104.50 per tonne fob Singapore. The trader said demand remained soft as supplies in Singapore have to compete with South Korean sellers for sale outlets.
Traders said demand from China were seen but bids were weak at $108 per tonne for delivery to southern China.

Other traders said fundamentals are healthy. They said India's latest tender to buy 50,000 tonnes of 180 cst fuel oil, in addition to its Monday's tender for 25,000 tonnes to be delivered in September, will support prices.
Traders said 180-cst fuel oil prices on Monday were quoted at $104.50/$106.
In the paper market, September was bid/asked at $104.50/$105 little changed from Monday's $105/$105.50.
